svg.title: AWS · Authorize the user, then write two kinds of data
svg.desc: An authenticated user calls application code. Code authorizes access, writes object bytes and then metadata using its workload identity. The writes are separate operations and need idempotency and partial-failure recovery.
svg.text: AWS · Authorize the user, then write two kinds of data
LOGICAL VIEW / private data access does not mean a private application endpoint
AWS workload ownership · logical services, not VPC placement
The application checks the end user. Lambda execution role grants the code only
the object and database operations it needs. A successful login is not a grant
If the object write succeeds but metadata fails, retry idempotently or
reconcile the orphan. For large files, issue a short-lived signed upload URL
after authorization; that alternate path is not drawn.
Solid arrows: labelled traffic or replication. Dashed arrows: policy/control. Conceptual design; assumptions and sources in the chapter.
